transcript: nice dark pad, bit too noisy, keep
why: The reference case. Proves 'bit' and 'too' are intensity qualifiers, NOT hedges - if they were, Noise would be suppressed.

transcript: I would keep the filter setting but cut the noise
why: Three independent defences all reject the verdict: 'keep the' is a carrier, 'would' is a hedge, and 'keep' is outside the trailing 6 tokens. 'cut the' shadows 'noise' so no Noise tag either - it is a request, not a description.

transcript: not dark
why: Suppress only, never invert. 'not dark' yields nothing and must NOT yield Bright. There is no antonym table in this design.

transcript: hard to tell
why: Carrier 'hard to' consumes its tokens and shadows 'tell'. No Hard.

transcript: short of ideas on this one
why: Carrier 'short of' consumes and shadows 'ideas'. No Short.

transcript: long time coming
why: Carrier 'long time' consumes and shadows 'coming'. No Long.

transcript: keep it in mind
why: The 3-token carrier 'keep it in' is checked before the lexicons and beats the 2-token verdict synonym 'keep it'. Carriers first, longest first.

transcript: having a hard time with this one
why: Carrier 'hard time'. No Hard.

transcript: as long as it holds up
why: 3-token carrier 'as long as' beats the 1-token Long key at the same position.

transcript: simple as that
why: Carrier 'simple as' consumes and shadows 'that'. No Simple.

transcript: it does not quiet down at all
why: Carrier 'quiet down', reinforced by the negator 'not'. No Quiet.

transcript: cut the noise please
why: The carrier shadow rule: 'cut the' consumes two tokens AND blocks the next one, so 'noise' cannot start a match. A request to reduce noise is not a Noise tag.

transcript: the high pass filter is doing a lot here
why: 'pass' is a meh synonym and would be a disaster in synth vocabulary without the 'high pass' carrier.

transcript: never mind that one
why: Carrier 'never mind' beats the verdict 'never'.

transcript: playing it in the key of C
why: Carriers 'the key' / 'key of' protect the keys Type. Bare 'key' is not in the lexicon either.

transcript: keep
why: A one-token utterance. Accepted by the trailing-6 clause at utterance scope; it is the <=4-token clause that carries it at segment scope.

transcript: meh
why: Bare verdict, second canonical value.

transcript: never again
why: A two-token utterance with an empty preceding window. The 2-token key beats the 1-token one at the same position.
Zero tokens. Must not crash, must return the empty proposal set.
Whitespace normalizes to zero tokens.

transcript: hmm
why: A single non-lexicon token yields nothing.

transcript: dark
why: Proves the empty-note gate (fewer than two alphabetic tokens) belongs to the CALLER, not to extract(). This note would never be persisted, but extraction is still correct.

transcript: maybe too bright
why: 'maybe' is two tokens before 'bright' - inside the 3-token window. Suppressed.

transcript: maybe a bit too bright
why: The other side of the same boundary: 'maybe' is FOUR tokens back, outside the window, so Bright survives. These two cases pin the window at exactly 3.

transcript: would be nice if it were brighter
why: 'if' at i-3 suppresses 'brighter'. A wish about a preset is not a description of it.

transcript: don't keep it
why: Contraction expansion makes 'do not keep it', and the negator 'not' at i-1 suppresses the verdict. Without expansion this would file the preset as keep - the exact opposite of what was said.

transcript: it's not noisy at all
why: Contraction expansion plus the negator window.

transcript: no, never
why: The negator window is applied uniformly, including to verdicts: 'no' at i-1 suppresses 'never'. Documented so the pedantic case is not a surprise.

transcript: I will never keep this
why: 'never' is deliberately in BOTH the negator set and the Verdict lexicon: it matches as the verdict AND suppresses the following 'keep this' one token later. Last-wins therefore settles on never, which is the correct reading.

transcript: harsh digital mess, never
why: Verdict never in the trailing-6 window with no blocker in front of it. Tags in first-appearance order.

transcript: keep this preset for the deep bass texture
why: 'keep this' starts at token 1 of 8, so the trailing-6 window (tokens 3-8) rejects it. No carrier and no hedge here - the positional rule is doing all the work. The Type still lands.

transcript: deep bass texture, keep this preset
why: Same words rearranged; 'keep this' now starts inside the trailing 6. Pins the window with its mirror case above.

transcript: sounds like a bass, actually more of a lead
why: Single-valued proposals are last-wins: a speaker correcting themselves means the second thing.

transcript: warm string ensemble, very soft, keep this one
why: Longest-match consumption: 'string ensemble' matches the strings Type and consumes 'ensemble', so the Ensemble characteristic must NOT also fire. 'warm' and 'soft' both map to Soft and dedupe to one tag.

transcript: weird vocoder thing, really bizarre
why: Two keys for one canonical value dedupe to a single tag; the span recorded is the first appearance.

transcript: huge cinematic pad, long release, quite dark, definitely a keeper
why: Realistic full sentence. 'long release' is a 2-gram so 'release' is consumed; 'quite' is an intensifier, not a hedge; 'a keeper' lands in the trailing 6.

transcript: really aggressive bass, way too harsh, never
why: Realistic full sentence. 'way' and 'too' are intensifiers, not hedges.

transcript: lovely ambient pad but not right for this track, come back to it later
why: A negator ('not') appears mid-sentence but only suppresses candidates that FOLLOW it within 3 tokens, so the earlier Ambient and pad survive. 'come back to' lands in the trailing 6.

transcript: acid lead, super funky, this is a keeper
why: Realistic full sentence with a trailing 'a keeper'.

transcript: bright organ, quite quiet in the mix, try it later
why: 'quite' and 'quiet' are distinct tokens and must not be confused. 'try it later' is a 3-token verdict key in the trailing 6.

transcript: crunchy digital percussion, short and snappy
why: 'short' and 'snappy' both map to Short and dedupe. No verdict anywhere in the utterance.

transcript: big brass section, very cinematic, long tail
why: 'brass section' and 'long tail' are 2-token keys; longest-match consumption keeps 'section' and 'tail' out of play.

transcript: deep sub bass, dark and simple
why: 'sub bass' is a 2-token Type key. Simple survives because no carrier or blocker precedes it.

transcript: just a riser, useless to me, never again
why: Two never candidates ('useless', then 'never again'); last-wins keeps the value the same but pins the span to the later one.

transcript: complex evolving texture with a lot going on
why: 'complex' and 'evolving' dedupe to one Complex. 'texture' is deliberately not a Type key.

transcript: generic little arp, nothing special
why: 'nothing' is a negator but the window is strictly preceding, so the 'nothing special' match does not suppress itself.

transcript: hard edged lead, love it
why: 'hard edged' is a legitimate 2-token Hard key and must not be caught by the 'hard to' / 'hard time' carriers.

transcript: just an init patch, nothing here
why: 'init patch' is a 2-token Type key. 'nothing here' is not a meh synonym - only 'nothing special' is, and near-misses must not fire.

transcript: short stabby percussion hits
why: 'short' and 'stabby' dedupe to Short.

transcript: no way, delete it
why: 'no way' matches with an empty preceding window; the later 'delete it' is suppressed by the negator 'no' at i-3, so last-wins settles on 'no way'. Same canonical value either way.

transcript: 8 bit chiptune lead, quite funky
why: Digits survive normalization: '8 bit' is a 2-token Digital key, deduped with 'chiptune'.

transcript: classic 303 bassline, squelchy as anything
why: '303' and 'squelchy' both map to Acid and dedupe.

transcript: DARK. Pad!! Keep.
why: Lowercasing and punctuation stripping happen before matching; the stored text stays verbatim regardless.

transcript: smooth mellow keys with a soft attack
why: 'smooth', 'mellow' and 'soft' all map to Soft and collapse to one tag. A purely descriptive utterance proposes no verdict.

transcript: wide unison pad, very lush
why: Ensemble fires as a characteristic when it is not consumed by the 'string ensemble' Type key. 'lush' is deliberately not in any lexicon.

transcript: hissy alien sound design, pretty bizarre
why: 'sound design' is a 2-token sfx key; 'alien' and 'bizarre' dedupe to Bizarre; 'pretty' is an intensifier, not a hedge.

transcript: I want it darker
why: 'want' is a hedge: a request for more darkness is not an assertion that the preset is Dark.

transcript: reduce the hiss a bit
why: 'reduce' is a negator, suppressing Noise two tokens later. Requests to change a preset are not descriptions of it.

transcript: get rid of the noise floor
why: 'get rid' is deliberately NOT a never synonym, and the 'rid of the' carrier shadows 'noise'. Removing noise from a preset is not rejecting the preset.

transcript: turn down the brightness on it
why: Pins the shadow width at exactly ONE token. 'turn down' consumes two and shadows 'the', but 'brightness' is two tokens past the carrier and survives. A known, accepted limit: widening the shadow would swallow real descriptions, so the answer is a longer carrier when a specific phrase proves noisy, never a wider shadow.

transcript: long release, short release
why: Both 'release' tokens are consumed by their 2-token keys, so neither can start another match. First-appearance order is Long then Short.

transcript: this is meh, actually keep it
why: Two verdict candidates in one utterance; last-wins takes 'keep it'. A speaker correcting themselves means the second thing.

transcript: honestly this is meh, actually no, keep it
why: Last-wins operates only over candidates that SURVIVED suppression. 'keep it' is killed by the negator 'no' at i-1, so the earlier 'meh' stands. Order of operations: suppress first, then last-wins.

transcript: SOUNDTRACK strings, very EPIC
why: Matching is case-insensitive but the emitted value is always the exact Arturia display string 'Soundtrack', never the user's casing.

transcript: decent pad, revisit
why: The emitted verdict is the wire slug 'try_later', never the display name 'Try later'.

transcript: okay so anyway that one there
why: A well-formed sentence with nothing in any lexicon must produce nothing rather than reaching for the nearest match.

transcript: cut the high pass on this one
why: CARRIERS CHAIN. 'cut the' consumes its tokens and shadows 'high'; the shadow forbids a LEXICON match there but must NOT forbid the 'high pass' carrier, or 'pass' is left bare and read as the 'meh' verdict. A request to cut the high-pass filter must never pre-aim a verdict chip.

transcript: lose the low pass resonance
why: Same chain with a different pair: 'lose the' shadows 'low', 'low pass' must still fire. Without carrier chaining this reads as the 'meh' verdict.

transcript: turn down the band pass a touch
why: 'turn down' shadows 'the'; 'the' starts no carrier and no lexicon key, so the scan reaches 'band pass' unshadowed anyway — the case is here to pin that chaining did not break the ordinary path.

transcript: hard to tell but keep it
why: Chaining must not weaken the shadow itself: 'hard to' still shadows 'tell', and no Hard tag is emitted. The trailing 'keep it' is inside the last six tokens and is still a verdict.
